The longest 40+ letter passage with the highest count is the refrain closing each of the seven letters to the churches (Revelation 2–3), "he who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches." It is 45 letters and occurs **7 times**.

This comes from reading the text by hand, not from running code. My shell commands never returned output, so no script counted the occurrences. I compared all seven occurrences letter by letter, but I couldn't mechanically check whether some other 40+ letter passage also appears 7 or more times.

The passage can't be made longer without losing an occurrence, because the letters on either side differ between occurrences:

- **Before it**, the letter differs (…amisw|, …zwhs|, …tosmou|, …prwinon|, …), so it can't be extended to the left.
- **After it**, the text continues as *twnikwn*, *onikwn*, *twnikwn*, *kaitwaggelw…* (three times) and *metatauta*, so it can't be extended to the right either.

Other refrains in the book repeat more often but are much shorter. For example, *eistousaiwnastwnaiwnwn* ("for ever and ever") is only 22 letters.
